name: Trees and overlapping sets
description: Three shared-geometry diagram layouts: reporting lines, a hierarchy, and overlapping sets. All examples are illustrative.

slides.title: Give the pilot a clear reporting structure
Break the pilot into focused workstreams
Three conditions for a useful pilot

org-chart.name: Organization chart
org-chart.summary: A single-root team structure, with reporting lines and child depths.
org-chart.description: Show one organization or reporting tree with 1 to 8 short entries. Use one list: the first entry is the level-zero root and each child sets its zero-based level. Keep parents before their children, without skipping a depth. Assistants and separate roots need a diagram instead; unsupported trees retain the complete list with a finding.

hierarchy.name: Hierarchy
hierarchy.summary: A single-root hierarchy drawn as connected pairs of rounded cards.
hierarchy.description: Show a classification or work breakdown with 1 to 8 short entries. Use one list: the first entry is the level-zero root and each child sets its zero-based level. Keep parents before children and do not skip a depth. Unsupported forests, jumps, descriptions or long labels retain the complete list with a finding instead of changing relationships or shrinking text.

venn.name: Venn
venn.summary: One to seven overlapping sets, with one short label per set.
venn.description: Show overlap among 1 to 7 sets using one flat list of short labels. The list order identifies the sets; no overlap values are implied. One to four sets have labels inside the circles, and five to seven beside them. Long labels, nested entries or unsupported counts retain the complete list with a finding instead of shrinking the text.
